idea-plugin.name: goome
idea-plugin.description:
Live templates, a new project action, a .goome.json preview and quick docs for goome. See-through overlays, normal app windows, game mod menus and engine ui. One file, no dependencies, Linux, Windows, Mac.

  • type goome in C, C#, Python, Java, Rust, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Zig, Lua or GDScript and pick a template, with the real names of each binding. C, C#, Python and Java use the same names as the VS Code extension
  • a goome tool window on the left, next to Project: quick actions, every .goome.json in the project, templates that start New Project with them picked, and a snippet cheat sheet
  • Tools > goome: New Project runs goome-cli with any of the ten templates (C, C#, Python, Java, Godot, Rust, Node, Go, Zig, Lua) and opens what it made
  • .goome.json and .goome-theme.json get checked against the goome schemas while you type
  • .goome.json opens with a live read only preview, plus buttons that copy the C, C#, Python, Java or GDScript code
  • Tools > goome: Build for Web runs goome build --web on a C app, then opens it in the browser through goome serve
  • Tools > goome: Update goome checks the project with goome upgrade --check, updates goome to the newest version when you press Update and offers to run the restore command afterwards
  • quick docs for goome_* C functions and the binding names in Rust, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Zig, Lua and GDScript, and goome: Search Docs everywhere

Works in Rider, CLion, IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, RustRover, GoLand and WebStorm, each gets the parts that fit it. Live templates need the plugin for that language: Rust, JavaScript, Go, ZigBrains, EmmyLua or Godot Support (built into Rider). Without it the plugin loads fine and skips them.

action.description: Make a goome project with goome-cli and open it
Find a goome function and open its docs
Open the goome UI builder in the browser
Compile the app to WebAssembly with goome build --web
Bump goome in this project to the newest version with goome upgrade
Stop the goome serve process started by Build for Web
